[H2] Evacuation Chairs for Stairs, Evacuation Sleds, and Rescue Stretchers

moves a person who cannot walk down the stairs safely when the elevators are out of service, during a fire, power outage, earthquake, or medical emergency. Anchortex carries Evac+Chair stair evacuation chairs, powered stair climbing chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories, along with Rapid Extraction (REX) rescue stretchers, for hospitals, nursing homes, schools, offices, high-rise buildings, and correctional facilities.

Most evac chair models are operated by one person: the passenger sits in a secure seat while the operator guides the chair down the stairs on tracks or belts that control the speed. Some models also carry a passenger up the stairs. An evacuation chair can be used in place of an evacuation wheelchair on stairs, where a standard wheelchair cannot go.

Evac+Chair 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs, with weight capacities from 400 to 500 lbs. The 600H and 750H also have extra handles so two people can carry a passenger up the stairs.
The battery powered Evac+Chair Power 800 and Power 900 carry a passenger up or down the stairs with one operator, for emergency evacuation and daily patient transport.
The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat lets two people move a patient up and down the stairs without carrying or heavy lifting.
The Evac+Sled, the Ulti-Mat (standard and bariatric sizes), and the Evac+Sheet rescue sheet, which stays under the mattress, for moving people who cannot sit, or bedridden patients, down the stairs.
REX ONE, REX DCS with descent control for stairs and steep ground, and REX DCS/CF for correctional facilities. Each folds in three for storage and lets one responder move a patient.
Comfy Seat cushions, the Transporter seat for transfers from a wheelchair, metal storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood.
[H2] How to Choose an Evacuation Chair
Check the rated capacity against the people who may need it. The 750H is rated to 500 lbs, and the Ulti-Mat comes in a bariatric size
Most models need one trained operator; some need two, and some allow two-person carrying when needed
Manual evacuation chairs are made for going down the stairs. For going up, choose a powered stair chair, the IBEX 700H, or a model with carry handles
Measure the stair landings and plan where each chair will be kept. Wall mounting and storage cabinets keep chairs close to the stairs and ready to use
Train staff on the chair, practice regularly, and include it in the building's emergency action plan
A lightweight, folding stair chair that lets one or two operators move a person with limited mobility down the stairs, and with some models up the stairs, during an emergency.
How many people does it take to operate an evac chair?
Most manual Evac+Chair models and the powered Power 800 and Power 900 need one operator. The IBEX 700H needs two. Models with carry handles can be lifted by two people.
Can an evacuation chair go up the stairs?
Yes, with the right model. The powered Power 800 and Power 900 and the IBEX 700H go up and down the stairs. The 600H and 750H can be carried up by two people.
Where should evacuation chairs be kept?
Near the stairways, on a wall mount or in a storage cabinet, so staff can reach them quickly.

is a correctional facility stretcher for jail and prison emergency response teams. It combines a folding rescue stretcher with built-in restraints and a descent control brake, so one officer can move an injured, ill, or restrained inmate across the facility, down the stairs, or out of the building in an emergency.

The tri-fold aluminum frame stores in a small space, is ready to roll in under 30 seconds, and has no components that can become weapons. Humane Restraint ankle and wrist cuffs attach easily to the frame
, and pre-installed straps hold the chest, waist, and legs
, so staff can move a restrained person safely and humanely with fewer officers.
Rugged T-6 aerospace aluminum with a tri-fold panel system
Ready to roll in under 30 seconds
Converts to a backboard, mobile stretcher, or patient treatment cot, and adjusts for supine and Fowler’s positions
Humane Restraint ankle and wrist cuffs that secure to the frame, plus pre-installed quick-release polypropylene chest, waist, and leg straps for full body restraint in incline and supine positions
Hand brake for controlled descent down stairs and steep ground; the parking brake keeps an unattended inmate from moving the stretcher; dual braking rods with an emergency auto-lock
Puncture-proof airless all-terrain tires on quick-release wheels
Flip-up headrest, adjustable pull handle, protective fenders, and front and rear kickstands
Designed and built in the USA
The REX DCS/CF suits jails, prisons, and detention centers that need to move inmates safely with fewer staff, whether the person is injured, ill, or resisting.
Restrain and move an inmate out of a cell and through the facility
Move injured inmates or officers to a point of care, from recreation injuries to mass-casualty incidents
Simple, low-profile patient loading and transport within the infirmary
Bring inmates down the stairs of multi-level buildings during a fire or other emergency
One officer can do work that would otherwise take several, freeing staff for other duties
Prison and Detention Hardware and Equipment
collections for more evacuation and restraint equipment.
Can one officer move a restrained inmate on the REX DCS/CF?
Yes. Once the inmate is restrained on the stretcher, a single officer can roll the REX DCS/CF through the facility and, with the descent control brake, down the stairs.
How is the REX DCS/CF different from the REX DCS?
The REX DCS/CF adds Humane Restraint ankle and wrist cuffs
and pre-installed chest, waist, and leg straps for full body restraint
, for use in correctional and detention facilities.
Can it be left with an inmate on board?
The parking brake keeps a restrained inmate from moving the stretcher by shifting their body weight. Follow your facility's policy for observing restrained inmates.

is a wheeled rescue litter with a built-in Descent Control System, so one responder can bring a patient down stairwells, steep grades, and rough ground at a controlled speed. It is the REX ONE multi-purpose extraction stretcher with an integrated hand brake, and it still converts into a backboard or a patient treatment cot.

Dual brake rods slow both wheels evenly from a single hand brake lever, and a safety lock button holds the brakes on without constant pressure, so the stretcher does not roll when it is stopped. Safety connection brackets and straps give responders extra control on difficult descents, which makes the REX DCS a practical stair stretcher for high-rise evacuations, mass casualty incidents, and EMS and fire teams.

How does the descent control brake work?
Squeeze the hand brake lever to slow both wheels through the dual brake rods. Press the safety lock button to hold the brakes on without keeping pressure on the lever.
Can one responder take a patient down the stairs?

Yes. The REX DCS is designed for a single responder, and the hand brake controls the speed on the way down. The safety connection brackets and straps let a second responder add control on difficult descents.
How is the REX DCS different from the REX ONE?
The REX DCS has the same tri-fold frame, configurations, and 400 lb capacity as the REX ONE, and adds the Descent Control System brake for stairs and steep terrain.
Is the REX DCS a rescue litter?
Yes, a wheeled one. Unlike a basket litter that a team carries, the REX DCS rolls on all-terrain wheels, brakes on the stairs, and folds into a backpack case.

is a multi-purpose rescue stretcher that lets a single responder move a patient quickly and safely over almost any terrain. The tri-fold mobile stretcher converts into a backboard or a patient treatment cot, so one device covers extraction, transport, and treatment for EMS, fire, law enforcement, and event medical teams.

Centered, balanced wheels and a telescoping pull handle give the REX ONE 360° maneuverability, and its 20” puncture-proof all-terrain tires need no maintenance. The evacuation stretcher is ready to roll in under 30 seconds and folds into a backpack carrying case, which makes it a good fit for mass casualty incidents, medical surge, HazMat operations, and active shooter response.
Rugged T-6 aerospace aluminum with a patented tri-fold panel system (head, center, and foot panels)
Converts to a backboard, mobile stretcher, or patient treatment cot, and adjusts for supine and Fowler’s positions

Move patients over rough ground, grass, gravel, and long distances to the ambulance

Can one person use the REX ONE?
Yes. The REX ONE is designed for rapid deployment by a single responder, and the balanced wheels and telescoping pull handle let one person move the patient.
Can the REX ONE go down the stairs?
For stairs and steep ground, choose the REX DCS. It is the REX ONE with a Descent Control System hand brake for controlled descent down stairwells and steep terrain.
What is the difference between standard and sand tires?
The standard 20” all-terrain tires are puncture-proof and handle most conditions. Sand tires are designed for beaches and sandy ground.
How is the REX ONE stored?
The rescue stretcher folds in three to 25”×18” and packs into its backpack carrying case, so it stows in a vehicle or closet and deploys quickly.

is a dual-position wheelchair evacuation chair that lets one operator move a person with limited mobility safely down the stairs in an emergency. It is used in place of an evacuation wheelchair on stairs, where a standard wheelchair cannot go, and its seat switches between a flat seat and a hammock seat to suit the passenger.

Self-braking Evac+Track friction tracks control the speed of descent, and fold-away front and rear grab handles let 2 to 4 people lift the chair for upward evacuation, such as from a basement, or through locations with difficult access. Is the Evac+Chair 600H an evacuation wheelchair?

It does the job of an evacuation wheelchair on the stairs. It is a folding evacuation chair, not an everyday wheelchair: the passenger moves into the chair, and the operator guides it down the stairs on its tracks.
Can the 600H go up the stairs?
Yes, with help. One operator takes the 600H down the stairs. For upward evacuation, 2 to 4 people use the fold-away front and rear grab handles to lift the chair up the stairs.
The seat can be used flat, with zipped side panels, or as a hammock seat by releasing the side panels and fastening them underneath. The over-thigh quick-release restraint works in both positions.
How is the 600H different from the 300H?
The 600H adds fold-away front and rear grab handles, so 2 to 4 people can carry it up the stairs or through difficult access. The 300H is the lighter standard model for downward evacuation.
